label: UniFi Switch Flex 2.5G PoE
description: Ubiquiti USW-Flex-2.5G-8-PoE - 8x 2.5GbE RJ45, every one a PoE++ PSE at the vendor's 64 W per-port ceiling, plus 1x 10GbE RJ45 that is the switch's PoE+++ power input rather than an output, and 1x 10G SFP+. PoE budget depends on how the box is fed: 196 W on the optional 210 W AC adapter, 76 W on a PoE+++ uplink, 46 W on PoE++, 16 W on PoE+.

poe.note: 196 W is the vendor's own maximum, and it needs the optional 210 W AC adapter: "Total PoE Availability: PoE+++ input: 76W / PoE++ input: 46W / PoE+ input: 16W / 210W AC adapter input: 196W" with "AC/DC adapter (Excluded)" under Power Method.

notes: All rows read from Ubiquiti's own tech-spec table on 2026-11-21 (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/switching/usw-flex-2-5g-8-poe, 200, 632,312 B, server-rendered): "Port Layout: 2.5 GbE RJ45 8 (All PoE++) (2.5G/1G/100M/10M) / 10 GbE RJ45 1 (PoE+++) (10G/5G/2.5G/1G/100M) / 10G SFP+ 1 (10G/1G)"; "PoE Ports: PoE++ 8"; "Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE: PoE 15.4W / PoE+ 32W / PoE++ 64W"; "Max. PoE Output: Up to PoE++"; "Power Method: (1) AC/DC adapter (Excluded), (1) PoE+++"; "Power Input Method: DC Input / PoE"; "Max. Power Consumption: 14W (Excluding PoE output) with PoE input, 17W with AC adapter input". The eight 2.5G sockets are all PoE++ per the vendor, so each declares the 64 W PSE ceiling rather than the 802.3af default the engine was deriving for every copper port. The 10G RJ45 socket is the box's power INLET, not a ninth PSE: the page lists it as "PoE+++" under Power Method and puts "Max. PoE Output" at PoE++ only, so it declares poeIn and no poeOut. The 90 W is the vendor's own arithmetic and not a standards guess - 76 W available to the eight ports plus 14 W maximum consumption with PoE input is exactly the 90 W an 802.3bt Type 4 source must supply. Ubiquiti prints availability, not input draw, so the input figure is derived from those two printed rows. No datasheet text layer exists for this SKU: https://dl.ui.com/ds/usw-flex-2-5g-8-poe_ds.pdf answers 200 with the 609,911-byte techspecs front page, so the table above is the only vendor surface.
